name: Hyperlipidemia due to Hepatic Triacylglycerol Lipase Deficiency

criteria.description: Persistent elevated serum triglyceride levels despite standard lipid-lowering therapy
Demonstrated deficiency or absence of hepatic triacylglycerol lipase enzymatic activity in liver biopsy or plasma
Identification of pathogenic variants in the LIPC gene encoding hepatic triacylglycerol lipase
Exclusion of secondary causes of hyperlipidemia such as diabetes mellitus, hypothyroidism, or nephrotic syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of elevated serum triglycerides with confirmed hepatic triacylglycerol lipase deficiency by enzymatic assay or genetic testing, and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily biochemical and genetic; liver biopsy is rarely performed.

laboratory: Reduced or absent hepatic triacylglycerol lipase enzymatic activity
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing hepatomegaly and hepatic steatosis
other: Liver biopsy rarely performed but may show lipid accumulation
Exclusion of secondary causes of hyperlipidemia

distinguishingFeatures: Deficiency of lipoprotein lipase enzyme instead of hepatic lipase
Early onset with eruptive xanthomas and pancreatitis

redFlags: Severe hypertriglyceridemia refractory to standard lipid-lowering therapies
Early onset xanthomas or hepatomegaly in absence of secondary causes
references: Brunzell JD, et al. Hepatic lipase deficiency and hyperlipidemia. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 1990.
Orphanet: Hyperlipidemia due to hepatic triacylglycerol lipase deficiency. ORPHA:140905.
Goldstein JL, Brown MS. The LDL receptor. Arterioscler Thromb Vasc Biol. 2009.
